exposure: Previous CS performed at a less equipped center
outcome: Scar complications (scar thinning, scar dehiscence, scar rupture)
Postoperative maternal complications (wound infections, blood transfusion reactions, psychiatric disturbances)
cohort: The study included 50 full-term pregnant women with a history of prior caesarean section who presented with scar tenderness and were selected for lower segment CS.
finding: 16.0% of the studied patients experienced scar dehiscence during repeat LSCS, with overall scar complications (thinning, dehiscence, rupture) observed in 46.0% of cases.
mod_finding: A short inter-delivery interval and a previous caesarean section performed at a less equipped center were significantly associated with scar complications.
